notes: v1.14.550 — LEGACY-RETIRE STAGE 6.5: KNOW AND HARDWARE, THE ENTANGLED PAIR, IN ONE SHIP. pg-power is split at source: its Runbook panel (pw-rb) is authored in #rf-know, and its strip plus the remaining five panels — Power, LED/GPU, Rack Map, BLAST RADIUS, Thermal — are authored in #rf-hw. redesign_homeKnow and redesign_homeHardware are both deleted (fifth and sixth of eight) and the pg-power shell goes with them. They had to ship together: as runtime moves they were ORDER-DEPENDENT, homeKnow taking pw-rb out before homeHardware drained the rest. Authored in source, that ordering problem stops existing rather than being preserved. ⛔ THREE RUNTIME EFFECTS THAT LEFT NO TRACE IN MARKUP had to be read out of the functions and baked in: pw-rb ships without its inline display:none and WITH stab-active (homeKnow set both); three stabs — Runbook, Rack Map, Blast Radius — ship with an inline display:none that homeHardware applied by a regex over their onclick attributes; and pw-rb is REMOVED from the STAB_GROUPS[pwr-sub] literal, which homeKnow used to strip at runtime. That last one has teeth: while pw-rb was still a member, switching any Hardware subtab stripped its stab-active and blanked the Know panel. ⚠ redesign_homeCompass (6.6) appends into #rf-hw .subtab-strip; that strip now exists in source from first paint, so its ordering dependency is satisfied unconditionally. VISIBLE UNDER ?legacy=1: the legacy house loses Power, LED/GPU, Thermal, BLAST RADIUS and the Runbook — the largest single loss of the campaign. The legacy hardware quick-action now says so instead of clicking a selector that matches nothing.
